rationales: Incorrect: financial data analysis is not the primary focus of biostatistics.
Correct: biostatistics applies statistical methods to biological and health-related sciences.
Incorrect: engineering models are not the primary subject of biostatistics.
Incorrect: studying historical events is the focus of history, not biostatistics.
Incorrect: designing experiments helps collect data but does not itself predict outcomes from current data.
Incorrect: drawing charts presents data visually but does not itself predict future outcomes.
Incorrect: taking an average summarizes data but does not generally predict future outcomes.
Correct: analysing data can reveal patterns and trends that are used to predict future outcomes.
Incorrect: the most frequently occurring value is the mode.
Incorrect: the middle value after ordering the data is the median.
Correct: the mean is the sum of all values divided by the number of values.
Incorrect: the difference between the highest and lowest values is the range.
Incorrect: 8 is the second value, not the middle value in the ordered data set.
Correct: 12 is the middle value of the five ordered values.
Incorrect: 15 is the fourth value, not the middle value.
Incorrect: 20 is the largest value, not the middle value.
Incorrect: 7 is the smallest value, not the mean.
Incorrect: the values sum to 45, which divided by 5 gives 9, not 8.
Correct: the sum is 45 and 45 divided by 5 is 9.
Incorrect: 10 is one of the data values, but the mean is 9.
Incorrect: with an even number of values there are two middle values, so one cannot simply choose a single middle value.
Correct: the median is the average of the two middle values after the data are ordered.
Incorrect: selecting the most frequent value gives the mode.
Incorrect: adding all values and dividing by their count gives the mean.
Incorrect: 3 occurs twice, which ties with 9 rather than making 3 the sole mode.
Incorrect: 6 occurs only once, so it is not a mode.
Incorrect: 7 occurs only once, so it is not a mode.
Correct: both 3 and 9 occur twice, more often than any other value.
Incorrect: the highest value is the maximum, not the mode.
Incorrect: the average of the data set is the mean, not the mode.
Correct: if no values repeat, no value occurs more often than the others, so there is no mode.
Incorrect: the median is the middle value, not the mode.
Incorrect: the number of categories is represented by the set of bars, not by each bar’s height or length.
Correct: each bar’s height or length represents the value for its corresponding category.
Incorrect: the average of all values is not what each individual bar represents.
Incorrect: the difference between the highest and lowest values is the range, not the meaning of a bar’s height or length.
Incorrect: the vertical axis usually represents values or frequencies, not categories.
Correct: categories are usually listed along the horizontal x-axis in a bar chart.
Incorrect: the axes generally have different roles rather than equally representing categories.
Incorrect: one axis—usually the horizontal axis—represents the categories.
